title: Python SDK: typed output guardrails, streaming checkpoints, and retry patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a pragmatic, backwards-compatible API in the Python SDK which makes structured outputs (pydantic/dataclass) ergonomic for both batched and streaming LLM responses, while codifying safe retry semantics and lightweight checkpointing for resumed streams. This ticket defines the API surface, in-SDK helper utilities, and a migration path for existing typed-response users.
acceptance_criteria: Library exposes two first-class adapters: TypedModelAdapter (pydantic) and DataclassAdapter (dataclass) that can hydrate streaming chunks incrementally.
Retry helper implements idempotency key propagation and a resume_token checkpoint format that the runtime can consume without coupling to transport layer.

Examples + tests show: a) synchronous generation with strict validation; b) streaming generator that yields partially hydrated objects; c) failure + resume flow with at-most-once semantic for side-effects.
Docs and migration guide added to /docs/sdk/python/typed-output.md and linked in the PR.
Performance regression < 5% p50 latency at small throughput (50 rps) for common chat workloads compared to untyped streaming baseline.

design_decisions: Expose two adapters rather than one multi-mode class: clearer single responsibility and simpler typed hints for users.
Default to validate_on_final_only to minimize runtime overhead for high-throughput workloads while providing an escape hatch for strict schemas.
Resume token is opaque and versioned (v1) to allow internal changes without breaking customers. Validators in SDK will reject tokens with unknown version.
RetryHelper will not automatically re-run user-defined side-effects. Instead SDK provides idempotency guidance and a helper wrapper to mark callables as idempotent for safe retries.
Use pydantic.BaseModel for the Pydantic path to leverage existing parsing/serialization, but keep a thin adapter layer so we can swap to pydantic v2 or an alternative in the future.
Avoid introducing new top-level exceptions; extend existing SDK exception hierarchy with TypedValidationError and ResumeError to keep consumer logic simple.
Keep API surface small: two main entrypoints in top-level package: typed_response.from_pydantic(...) and typed_response.from_dataclass(...).
implementation_notes: Key files touched: src/typed_response/adapter.py, src/typed_response/retry.py, examples/typed_stream_resume.ipynb. New tests under tests/typed_response/test_stream_resume.py. The resume token serializer lives in src/typed_response/token.py and uses compact base64-encoded JSON with a version prefix. Unit tests exercise token forward/backward compatibility and invalid token rejection.
code_examples:
# Synchronous usage:
from redwood import typed_response
from models import ChatCompletionModel

response = client.generate(... )
obj = typed_response.from_pydantic(ChatCompletionModel, response)
# obj is fully validated pydantic model on completion

# Streaming usage with resume + minimal validation:
from redwood import typed_response, RetryHelper

stream = client.stream_generate(...)
adapter = typed_response.from_dataclass(MyChatSchema, validate_on_final_only=True)
for partial in adapter.stream_hydrate(stream):
    if partial.complete:
        final_obj = partial.value
        break
    else:
        # show partial.text to user without full validation
        display(partial.fields.get('text'))

# In case of transport hiccup, RetryHelper.resume(stream, resume_token) will request resume from runtime using token stored by adapter.
